top_story_title: Zyxel GS1900 switches: the patch everyone applied fixed the wrong bug, and ~1,000 switches were taken over
top_story_summary: Binarly reports that the exploitation of Zyxel GS1900 series switches seen in the wild did not use CVE-2026-7273, the stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI program that Zyxel advised on in June 2026 and that CISA added to the KEV catalog on 2026-09-21. It used a separate, then-unknown out-of-bounds write now tracked as CVE-2026-107441. Switches that took the earlier fix and were considered closed out stayed exploitable the whole time.
top_actions: Inventory every GS1900 in the estate by model and firmware; the earlier fix for CVE-2026-7273 does not protect against CVE-2026-107441, so firmware date alone is not a clean bill of health.
Block reachability of the GS1900 web management interface from all user, guest and internet-facing segments immediately - management ACL or an upstream firewall rule to the management VLAN only.
Apply the new Zyxel firmware for the affected GS1900 models; confirm the fixed release for your exact model against the vendor advisory rather than assuming a build number.

Treat any exposed GS1900 as config-compromised: rotate local admin passwords, SNMP community strings, RADIUS/TACACS+ shared secrets and any credential that appears in the switch config, including anywhere else those credentials were reused.
Export and diff the running config against a known-good copy - look for added admin accounts, changed VLAN or port assignments, new static routes, altered DNS or syslog destinations.
executive_summary: Zyxel GS1900 switches: in-the-wild exploitation used CVE-2026-107441, not the KEV-listed CVE-2026-7273 that was patched in June - roughly 1,000 switches compromised and their configs and credentials stolen. New firmware is out for 10 models. Patch, then rotate everything in the config.

Cisco's November 4 batch: UCS Central RCE (CVE-2026-76506, 7.6), Unified CM XSS (CVE-2026-76419, 6.1), ISE authorization bypass (CVE-2026-20241, 5.3). ISE and UCS Central are management-plane assets - prioritise them over the XSS.
Cisco's October Node.js roundup carries a KEV entry: CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, with a CISA BOD 26-04 due date of 2026-11-10.

SonicWall will not patch two flaws in end-of-life GMS 9.5.2 and earlier, one an unauthenticated file read at CVSS 9.1. There is no upgrade path on that software - it has to come off the network or move behind strict controls.
Barracuda Email Security Gateway: an authentication bypass chains with a command injection for root on the appliance.
Nothing in this window is a genuine AI-and-network-gear story; the two AI items collected concern AI coding agents and ChatGPT, not network devices.
key_actions: **Zyxel** — Upgrade affected GS1900 switches to the new Zyxel firmware for your model; verify the image against the vendor hash before loading.
**Zyxel** — Restrict the management plane: web GUI and SSH reachable only from the management VLAN via a management ACL, never from user, guest or internet-facing segments.
**Zyxel** — Re-open the June remediation record for every GS1900: the earlier firmware does not address the exploited flaw.
**Zyxel** — Apply the new firmware for the affected models; stage the access layer in maintenance windows after confirming the fixed release for each model against the vendor advisory.
**Zyxel** — Track CVE-2026-107441 as a distinct remediation item from CVE-2026-7273; do not close one on the evidence of the other.
**Zyxel** — Confirm the running firmware of each GS1900 against the vendor's fixed-release table for CVE-2026-107441 specifically.
**Zyxel** — Upgrade to the fixed firmware for your GS1900 model per the vendor advisory.
**Zyxel** — Apply management ACLs so only the management VLAN can reach the switch's HTTP/HTTPS interface; disable HTTP entirely where the model allows.

headlines.title: Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
headlines.summary: Zyxel patched a zero-day in GS1900 series switches that attackers used to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configuration files and credentials.

headlines.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
headlines.summary: Zyxel's earlier GS1900 fix did not close the flaw attackers were actually using; unauthenticated command execution via the web management interface remained open until new firmware shipped.

headlines.title: Patched Zyxel GS1900 switches remained open to in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441)
headlines.summary: The June fix for Zyxel GS1900 switches addressed CVE-2026-7273 while the in-the-wild exploit relied on a different bug, CVE-2026-107441, which stayed unpatched.

headlines.title: Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-107441 is an out-of-bounds write in Zyxel GS1900 switches that allows OS command execution via crafted HTTP requests.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October 2026 Node.js advisory covers four High-rated flaws in its products, including KEV-listed CVE-2026-111497 in the Brotli decoder with a CISA due date of 2026-11-10.

headlines.title: SonicWall Won't Patch EoL GMS Flaws That Could Expose Files, Alter Database Records
headlines.summary: SonicWall will not patch two flaws in end-of-life GMS 9.5.2 and earlier, including CVE-2026-109593, an unauthenticated file read rated CVSS 9.1.
